The non-persistence is the decision, not an omission. `migrateLegacy` runs at module load, which is before `useGallonStandardSync`'s `/settings/public` fetch resolves, and an absent gallon key falls back to `us`; persisting that guess froze it, because every later path is guarded on `unit_prefs` being ABSENT and `setGallonStandard` notifies only its own listeners, so nothing could heal the record. That was reachable on a UK instance whose first post-upgrade settings fetch fails (the key is never written on US instances, so its absence is indistinguishable from normal) and on any instance whose admin later switches the published flavour, and it left every volume and MPG about twenty percent wrong permanently. Not persisting keeps the legacy keys authoritative until the client makes a real choice through `setUnitPrefs`, which does persist. THAT SENTENCE USED TO END 'so rung 2 still follows the server the way it did before the store existed', and the fix round after task 5 corrected it: rung 2 followed the server only because `useGallonStandardSync` rewrote `imperial_gallon_standard` from `/settings/public` on every boot, and task 5 deleted that writer. Closing it needs the live instance default, which this module cannot see, so the record now carries the flag and `useUnitPreference` rung 2 acts on it (see below). The claim this sentence used to make, that no browser's rendered units move, was false for exactly that population and the persist was pinned by no test at all: deleting it broke zero. `utils/__tests__/unitPrefsStore.test.ts` now fails when it is restored. When task 5 retires the legacy keys it must write the record through `setUnitPrefs` rather than assume the migration left one behind. (2) `presetTagFor` (MOVED to `types/units.ts` by phase 4 task 4, because the settings card needs the identical rule and a second copy of it is how this workstream started) names a set `custom` unless it is exactly the preset for its binary system, which is migration 093's `_materialise_uk_imperial_users` rule stated generally: the imperial and metric presets are both written with `secondary_gallon='us'`, so a UK-gallon browser is custom whichever preset it started from. Deriving the tag rather than storing it means the settings card cannot highlight a preset over a set that is not it. (3) `readLegacySystem` carries the `units-exempt(compare)` pragma that used to sit in `hooks/useUnitPreference.ts::readStoredUnitSystem`; it moved with the read it excuses and the suppression count is unchanged, which `utils/__tests__/unitsBinaryApiSurface.test.ts` pins by exact list. The lenience the header argues for is unchanged; only the number was stale, and a stale number is what this phase keeps finding. Task 4's review found the SECOND DOOR onto the same defect and it is closed here: withholding the set inside `migrateLegacy` is not sufficient, because a later modifier-only write that persisted `current.units` froze the same module-load gallon guess as a side effect of a DISPLAY DENSITY toggle.
